purpose: Evidence map and unresolved research agenda.

sources.title: Measures of financial toxicity in cancer survivors
sources.synthesis: Cancer-related financial toxicity is multidimensional and should be assessed beyond a single cost question.

sources.title: Systematic Review of Fear of Cancer Recurrence Patient-Reported Outcome Measures
sources.synthesis: Fear of recurrence is a distinct survivorship concern that warrants explicit assessment rather than being folded into generic anxiety.

sources.title: Cancer-related cognitive impairment: updates to treatment, management, and clinical guidance
sources.synthesis: Cancer-related cognitive impairment can affect everyday function, work ability, productivity and quality of life.

sources.title: Experiences of financial toxicity among caregivers of patients with cancer
sources.synthesis: Cancer-related financial burden extends to caregivers and can reshape ordinary household life.

sources.title: When Breath Becomes Air
sources.synthesis: Paul Kalanithi's memoir offers narrative insight into terminal illness, professional identity, family and meaning; it is not clinical efficacy evidence.

sources.title: The impact of adverse childhood experiences on multimorbidity
sources.synthesis: Review evidence links greater childhood adversity exposure with later long-term conditions and multimorbidity, while individual causal attribution remains inappropriate.

sources.title: Posttraumatic stress disorder in the World Mental Health Surveys
sources.synthesis: Cross-national findings reinforce that trauma exposure does not automatically produce PTSD and that persistence and treatment access vary.

sources.title: What is the impact of mental health-related stigma on help-seeking for mental health problems?
sources.synthesis: Stigma can deter help-seeking, making anticipated discrimination a relevant access variable.

sources.title: Ableism within health care professions: a systematic review
sources.synthesis: The review documents ableism and discrimination within healthcare workplaces and training, illustrating secondary harms created by systems rather than impairment alone.

evidence_hierarchy: Prefer systematic reviews/meta-analyses for broad population claims when quality is adequate.
Use government and specialty guidance for current terminology, safety and clinical framing.
Use qualitative and patient-reported research to identify lived-experience domains that quantitative endpoints can miss.
Use memoirs, books and documentaries as contextual evidence, never as prevalence or causal evidence.
Assess recency, study design, sample, bias, heterogeneity and population relevance rather than ranking by publication date alone.
causation_guardrails: Association is not proof of individual causation.
Bidirectional relationships are common between health, mental health, work, housing and relationships.
Pain, sleep, medications, endocrine/neurological factors, poverty, discrimination and access can confound observed relationships.
ACE counts are not destiny and do not capture the full meaning, severity or context of adversity.
A diagnosis or event must not be used to predict one person's prognosis without person-specific evidence.
copyright_rules: Do not reproduce copyrighted articles, books, films or long passages.
Store bibliographic metadata and original paraphrased synthesis.
Keep URLs so downstream systems can retrieve or verify sources where legally available.
Do not transform narrative sources into clinical facts.
